title: Hash table
summary: A hash table maps keys to values using a hash function. Structure: array of buckets, each holding a list of entries (chaining) or a single entry (open addressing). Load factor = entries/buckets. Resize when load factor exceeds threshold (typically 0.75). Hash functions: division method (h(k) = k mod m), multiplication method, universal hashing. Collision resolution: chaining (linked lists), open addressing (linear probing, quadratic probing, double hashing, Robin Hood hashing).

ext.summary: A hash table maps keys to values using a hash function. Structure: array of buckets, each holding a list of entries (chaining) or a single entry (open addressing). Load factor = entries/buckets. Resize when load factor exceeds threshold (typically 0.75). Hash functions: division method (h(k) = k mod m), multiplication method, universal hashing. Collision resolution: chaining (linked lists), open addressing (linear probing, quadratic probing, double hashing, Robin Hood hashing).

structure.meaning: Maps key to bucket index: h(k) = k mod m (division), or h(k) = floor(m * (k * A mod 1)) (multiplication), or universal hashing.
Each bucket is a linked list of entries. Simple but has cache-unfriendly pointer chasing.
On collision, try (h(k)+i) mod m for i=0,1,2,... (primary clustering).
On collision, try (h(k)+i^2) mod m (reduces clustering).
On collision, try (h1(k) + i*h2(k)) mod m (best distribution).
On collision, swap if the new entry has traveled farther than the existing one. Improves worst-case.
α = n/m (entries/buckets). Resize when α > threshold (0.75 for chaining, 0.5 for open addressing).
Allocate new array (2x), rehash all entries. Amortized O(1) per insert.

notes: Hash tables provide O(1) average-case lookup, insert, and delete.
Hash tables are used in caches, symbol tables, databases, and many algorithms.
Cryptographic hash functions (SHA-256) are not suitable for hash tables (too slow).
Universal hashing provides worst-case guarantees (O(1) expected).
Consistent hashing is used in distributed systems (Dynamo, Cassandra).
